SMTO-HTTP-0078 — HTTP request failed

GUID: fe34db55-a534-4d09-9c2e-d366262b071c
Slug: http-request-failed
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO's request to a web service didn't finish with a usable answer, and SMTO didn't try again on its own. If the request was meant to change something, that change may or may not have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at this step in the conversation for a more specific message next to this one, or open Technical details in this panel. This is a general message; the more specific one names the actual cause.
  2. If the request was meant to change something, such as creating, updating, sending or deleting, check in the service itself whether that change is already there. The request may have reached the service even though SMTO never got a complete answer.
  3. Only if the change isn't there, or the request only read information, ask SMTO in the conversation to try the request again. Checking first keeps the same change from being made twice.

What success looks like

  • The service shows the result you expected, only once, and the step finishes with a reply.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or the service. Don't repeat a change until you've confirmed it didn't already happen.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway HTTP client returned a generic failure: the request did not produce an accepted, complete result, and no automatic retry was performed.

What this means

  • The generic HTTP failure message is used by _failure for many specific error kinds; it establishes no cause beyond the missing accepted complete result. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The generic HTTP failure message is used by _failure for many specific error kinds; it establishes no cause beyond the missing accepted complete result.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect error_kind, failure_class, executed, complete and effect_unknown in the same receipt.

How to fix it

  • Read error_kind, executed and effect_unknown in the HTTP receipt (built by _failure in gateway_core/http_client.py); this generic message does not tell us what caused the failure. For write methods with effect_unknown, check the target's current state before any new attempt.
  • Inspect the specific error kind and execution facts in the receipt before choosing a corrective action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The specific failure condition is resolved and any earlier uncertain mutation is settled.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
